nasa_record.title: Lake Mead Drops to a Record Low

earthdata_2026.title: Low Water Levels in Lake Powell and Lake Mead in August 2026

claims.text: Everything in orange was underwater in 2000.

evidence.method: orange = water mask of 2000-07-06 minus water mask of 2026-07-30, same 30 m grid (yt-geo watermask.py)

claims.text: Lake Mead is America's largest reservoir.
claims.quote: Lake Mead is the largest reservoir in the United States
claims.verification: WebSearch restricted to nasa.gov/usbr.gov/usgs.gov/nps.gov (search-engine excerpts of these pages); direct page fetch is blocked by this environment's egress policy

claims.text: Since 2000, its surface has dropped about 160 feet (about 49 m).
claims.quote: end of July 2000: 1,199.97 feet; August 2026: 1,039.77 feet (USBR)
claims.verification: WebSearch restricted to nasa.gov/usbr.gov/usgs.gov/nps.gov (search-engine excerpts of these pages); direct page fetch is blocked by this environment's egress policy

claims.text: Its northern arm pulled back about nine miles (about 14 km).

evidence.method: northernmost water pixel of the Overton Arm (columns 1300-1800): row 432 (2000) vs 912 (2026) x 30 m = 14.4 km = 8.9 mi

claims.text: In 2022, it hit its lowest level since it was first filled in the 1930s.
claims.quote: July 2022: lowest level since the lake began filling in the 1930s (about 1,040 ft)
claims.verification: WebSearch restricted to nasa.gov/usbr.gov/usgs.gov/nps.gov (search-engine excerpts of these pages); direct page fetch is blocked by this environment's egress policy

claims.text: About half of its surface water is gone.

evidence.method: water-mask pixels over the whole lake (the stack area covers all of Lake Mead): 296,190 (2026-07-30) / 579,141 (2000-07-06) = 0.51; display-aid classification, hence 'about half'

claims.text: A long drought on the Colorado River.
claims.quote: since the onset of the current drought in 2000, Lake Powell and Lake Mead have fallen to historically low elevations
